name: vibedev_scaffold_directive
content: Your working directory is a NEW, uninitialized project: it has no app yet (no package.json / Cargo.toml / pyproject.toml / index.html). You MUST scaffold a working starter into the CURRENT directory BEFORE implementing the request below.

- If the build request names a stack or framework (e.g. Next.js, SvelteKit, Vue, Remix, Nuxt, Astro, Vite, a Rust crate, a Python project), scaffold it with that stack's official non-interactive create tool INTO the current directory (`.`) — e.g. `npx create-next-app@latest . --yes`, `npm create svelte@latest .`, `npm create vite@latest . -- --template <t>`, `cargo init`, etc. Pick non-interactive flags so it never blocks on a prompt.

- If NO stack is named, create a sensible minimal generic starter that fits the request's intent and language (default to a small Vite/Node web app, or a single static `index.html` for a simple page).
- Scaffold INTO the current working directory; do not nest the app inside an extra subfolder.
- After scaffolding, implement the actual request against the new starter and make sure the project's dev/build command runs.
Then proceed with the build request:

metadata.description: Server-authoritative VibeDev scaffold directive. Prepended to a Pi coding run by run_coding_task when the bound project repo is an empty/uninitialized isolated dir (no recognized manifest, first build of the chain, not the shared workspace root, not a plan run). Lets Pi pick the create tool from the stack named in the build request, with a generic fallback, so greenfield 'build me an app' prompts scaffold instead of stalling with no_change.
metadata.author: magician
metadata.changelog: v1.0.0: Initial scaffold-on-empty directive for isolated greenfield VibeDev projects.
